# Code of Conduct

Seed Code CLI is an open-source developer tool with a community around it:
issue trackers, discussions, pull requests, and any other project space. This
document describes the behaviour expected of everyone who takes part, and what
happens when it is not met. It applies to maintainers and contributors alike.

## Our commitment

We want participation in this project to be a safe, respectful and productive
experience for everyone, regardless of experience level, background, identity,
or the tools and platforms they use. Technical disagreement is welcome and
expected; personal hostility is not.

## Expected behaviour

- **Communicate respectfully.** Assume good faith, keep criticism about the
  code or the idea rather than the person, and write as though the other person
  is reading carefully — because they are.
- **Collaborate constructively.** Offer concrete detail: what you expected,
  what happened, how to reproduce it, and what you already tried. A precise bug
  report or a focused pull request is a contribution in itself.
- **Be patient and inclusive.** Not everyone has the same experience,
  language, timezone or available time. Explain rather than dismiss, and avoid
  jargon where plain language works.
- **Give and accept feedback gracefully.** Review the change, not the person.
  If a review is unclear, ask for specifics instead of escalating.
- **Respect boundaries and privacy.** Do not publish someone else's private
  information, credentials, project data, or correspondence without their
  explicit permission.

## Unacceptable behaviour

The following is not tolerated in any project space:

- Harassment, intimidation, or sustained disruption of discussions.
- Discrimination, hate speech, or slurs of any kind, including on the basis of
  race, ethnicity, nationality, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual
  orientation, disability, age, religion, or experience level.
- Threats of violence, or encouragement of violence or self-harm.
- Personal attacks, insults, or deliberately demeaning comments.
- Sexualised language or imagery, or unwelcome sexual attention.
- Publishing another person's private information without permission.
- Spam, deliberate derailing, or repeated bad-faith argument.
- Knowingly submitting code that is malicious, that hides data collection or
  telemetry, or that introduces undisclosed credentials or backdoors.

## Scope

This code applies in all project spaces — the repository, issues, pull
requests, discussions, review comments, and any public channel where someone is
representing the project. It also applies when an individual is officially
representing the project elsewhere.

## Maintainer responsibilities

Maintainers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing these standards. They
should:

- lead by example and model the behaviour described above;
- apply the same standards to their own conduct as to everyone else's;
- respond to reports promptly, fairly and consistently;
- keep a reported incident confidential, and recuse themselves from handling a
  report in which they are personally involved;
- take any action they consider appropriate, up to and including a permanent
  ban, when behaviour is unacceptable.

Maintainers may remove, edit or reject comments, commits, code, issues and
other contributions that do not follow this code, and will explain the reason
where it is useful to do so.

## Reporting

If you experience or witness unacceptable behaviour, report it privately rather
than escalating publicly. This project does not publish a dedicated conduct
email address; please use a **private** channel that reaches the maintainers,
such as the repository's private reporting facilities, or a direct private
message to a maintainer through the platform where you are interacting with the
project.

When reporting, include as much of the following as you are comfortable
sharing: what happened, where and when it happened, who was involved, and any
links or screenshots. **Do not paste API keys, tokens, passwords, or other
credentials into a report** — redact them first.

Reporters' privacy is respected: a report is shared only with the maintainers
who need it to assess and act on it, and the identity of a reporter is not
disclosed without their consent, except where required by law.

## Enforcement

Reports are reviewed by the maintainers. Depending on severity and history,
consequences may include:

1. a private warning with an explanation of what was unacceptable;
2. a request to edit or remove the offending content;
3. a temporary restriction from project spaces;
4. a permanent ban from participation.

Deliberately false or malicious reports are themselves a violation of this
code. Good-faith reports, even if they turn out to be mistaken, are always
welcome and will not be penalised.

## Attribution

This code of conduct is maintained by the Seed Code CLI project and may be
updated as the community grows. Continued participation after an update means
accepting the current version.
